claims.text: The initial material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy containing dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Additive manufacturing can produce a refined microstructure in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The additive-manufactured microstructure will have fewer internal boundaries.
Additive manufacturing will optimize the phase distribution.
Additive manufacturing permits precise control over the alloy microstructure.
The microstructure produced by additive manufacturing can reduce microcracking during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Reduced microcracking will enhance room-temperature tensile ductility.
Additive manufacturing can maintain or increase tensile strength while enhancing ductility.
Additive-manufactured eutectic high-entropy alloys will exhibit greater tensile strength than conventionally processed counterparts.
Additive-manufactured eutectic high-entropy alloys will exhibit greater elongation or tensile ductility than conventionally processed counterparts.
Conventional processing of eutectic high-entropy alloys increases strength but reduces ductility.
The expected improvements may depend on additive-manufacturing parameters and alloy composition.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in both strength and ductility relative to a conventionally processed control would falsify the hypothesis.
